description: SHELL PINCH-BOUNDARY GOLDEN (SH-1, docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md 2026-07-30) — the SOUND side of the zero-width-slit threshold, one step below it. Body: the CM-4 layout (40x40x10 plate -> [4,12]x[10,30] through-pocket -> r3 fillet on every Z-parallel edge), shelled to a 1.9 mm wall with the TOP face open. The rib between the outer wall and the pocket wall is 4.0 mm, so this shell's two inward offsets (outer x=0 -> x=1.9, pocket x=4 -> x=2.1) come within 0.2 mm of each other WITHOUT touching: the cavity survives as a 0.2 mm-wide slot and the body is sound. At t=2.0 mm exactly they land on the same plane, the cavity pinches to zero width, and shell_body refuses the body with shell_thickness_too_large (test_shell.py::test_thickness_that_pinches_a_rib_to_zero_width_is_refused); at t=2.1 mm the two walls merge into solid material and the body is sound again. This golden is the analytic anchor of that threshold: it proves the guard DISCRIMINATES (a 0.1 mm-thinner wall builds, byte-deterministically) instead of merely firing. It also locks the tolerance-bearing case of the shell verb on curved geometry — 16 quarter-cylinders (r 1.1 / 3.0 / 4.9) in one body, three offset radii of the same r3 fillet.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED closed forms (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug); the harness residual against each is quoted in tolerance_rationale. Symbols: t = 1.9 mm wall, plate 40x40x10, pocket P = [4,12]x[10,30] through, r = 3 mm fillet on all Z edges.

PLAN AREA. Filleting all four corners of a w x h rectangle with radius r removes r^2(4 - pi). Outer plan = 1600 - 9(4 - pi) = 1564 + 9pi; the pocket hole = 160 - 9(4 - pi) = 124 + 9pi. Material plan = (1564 + 9pi) - (124 + 9pi) = 1440 EXACTLY — the two roundings cancel because both use r=3, which is why the pre-shell volume is exactly 14400 mm^3 with no pi term.

CAVITY PLAN. The inward offset is a Minkowski erosion of the material plan by t (build123d hollow uses the ARC join, so every offset corner is a true arc — the arcs below are that join, verified by the residual). Eroding the outer boundary shrinks the 40x40 rectangle to (40 - 2t) and its corners from r to (r - t): eroded = (40 - 2t)^2 - (r - t)^2(4 - pi) = 36.2^2 - 1.21(4 - pi) = 1305.6 + 1.21pi = 1309.4013271108440. Dilating the pocket grows it to (8 + 2t) x (20 + 2t) with corners (r + t): dilated = 11.8 x 23.8 - 24.01(4 - pi) = 184.8 + 24.01pi = 260.2296396126910. The dilated pocket lies wholly inside the eroded outer region (x in [2.1,13.9], y in [8.1,31.9]) and its left face sits 0.2 mm clear of the eroded outer wall at x=1.9 — the pinch gap. cavity plan = 1305.6 + 1.21pi - 184.8 - 24.01pi = 1120.8 - 22.8pi = 1049.1716874981530.

VOLUME. The cavity is prismatic (every offset here is vertical) from the floor z=t to the OPEN top z=10, so height 10 - t = 8.1: cavity = 8.1(1120.8 - 22.8pi) = 9078.48 - 184.68pi = 8498.2906687350390. volume = 14400 - cavity = 5321.52 + 184.68pi = 5901.7093312649610 mm^3.

SURFACE AREA, face group by face group. Perimeter of a fillet-cornered rectangle = 2(w - 2r) + 2(h - 2r) + 2pi r. Outer skin: (4 x 34 + 6pi) x 10 = 1360 + 60pi. Pocket skin: (2 x 2 + 2 x 14 + 6pi) x 10 = 320 + 60pi. Bottom z=0: the material plan, 1440. Top z=10: the material plan MINUS the cavity opening = 1440 - (1120.8 - 22.8pi) = 390.8283125018474 (two faces: the outer rim frame and the ring around the pocket). Cavity floor z=1.9: 1049.1716874981530. Cavity outer wall: perimeter of the eroded boundary (4 x 34 + 2pi x 1.1) x 8.1 = 1101.6 + 17.82pi. Cavity inner wall: (2 x 2 + 2 x 14 + 2pi x 4.9) x 8.1 = 259.2 + 79.38pi. Total = 5920.8 + 217.2pi = 6603.1539243597030 mm^2.

CENTROID. y = 20.0 EXACTLY by the surviving mirror symmetry about y=20 (the pocket spans y in [10,30], centred). z: the body is the 10 mm prism (V 14400, centroid z 5) minus the cavity prism (V 8498.2906687350390, centroid z (1.9 + 10)/2 = 5.95), so z = (72000 - 8498.2906687350390 x 5.95)/5901.7093312649610 = 3.6320274886245790. x: first plan moments about x=0. The outer plan and the eroded outer plan are symmetric about x=20; the pocket and its dilation about x=8. plan moment of the material = 20(1564 + 9pi) - 8(124 + 9pi) = 30288 + 108pi; of the cavity = 20 x 1309.4013271108440 - 8 x 260.2296396126910. x = [10(30288 + 108pi) - 8.1(20 x eroded - 8 x dilated)]/volume = 18.8102767333389500.
BOUNDING BOX = [0,0,0]..[40,40,10]: an INWARD shell leaves the outer envelope untouched and the r3 fillets are tangent to the original faces, so the extent is the raw plate's.

TOPOLOGY, enumerated: 36 faces = outer skin 8 (4 planes + 4 r3 cylinders) + pocket skin 8 (4 + 4 r3) + bottom 1 (one face, inner loop = the pocket) + top 2 (the outer rim frame and the ring around the pocket, each with an inner loop) + cavity floor 1 (inner loop = the dilated pocket) + cavity outer wall 8 (4 planes + 4 cylinders at r - t = 1.1) + cavity inner wall 8 (4 planes + 4 cylinders at r + t = 4.9). 96 edges = bottom loops 8 + 8, top loops 8 + 8 (outer, pocket) + 8 + 8 (cavity outer, cavity inner), cavity-floor loops 8 + 8, and 4 sets of 8 vertical edges = 16 + 32 + 16 + 32. 1 shell (the cavity is open to the top, so the body has a single boundary shell). Cross-check: 64 vertices = 16 (bottom) + 32 (top) + 16 (cavity floor), the count the kernel reports.

MESH (linear 0.1 mm, angular 0.1 rad): 2176 vertices / 2112 triangles, RECORDED from the tessellator rather than hand-derived — the arc subdivision is analytic (angular deflection 0.1 rad puts ceil((pi/2)/0.1) = 16 segments on every quarter arc, and it is the angular limit that binds, cross-checked by a bare cylinder tessellating to the same 506/500 at r = 1.1, 3.0 and 4.9), but the Delaunay triangulation of the six planar faces whose boundaries carry those arcs is OCCT's, not a closed form. They are asserted EXACTLY as a regression pin (a changed count is a real geometric change) and the runner's two determinism legs — in-process rebuild and fresh-interpreter rebuild — prove they are not run-dependent. GLB byte size is deliberately not pinned (glTF-writer upgrades).
tolerance_rationale: CURVED-composition tier, reused verbatim from docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md's documented CURVED_TOL = 1e-8 (the tier pattern-cut-6hole-boltcircle-60x60x10 / mirror-hole-feature-plate-40x40x20 carry; that class's documented worst residual is 2.4e-11) — measured first, then set, never widened to go green. Measured deviations of the harness from the closed forms above (2026-07-30, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0): volume 5.46e-12 mm^3, surface_area 2.73e-12 mm^2, centroid.x 7.11e-15 mm, centroid.y 3.55e-15 mm, centroid.z 4.44e-16 mm, AABB min 4.44e-16 mm (the sketch solve puts the plate corner at -4.4e-16, not 0.0). Worst case 5.46e-12 leaves ~1800x headroom. NOT the planar 1e-9 tier: this body carries 16 cylindrical faces at three different radii and four composed ops (extrude, cut, fillet, shell), and the closed form itself moves by ~2e-12 purely from summation order (5901.709331264961 vs ...963 when the pi terms are collected differently), so a 1e-9 bound would sit only ~180x above a residual that is partly arithmetic bookkeeping. Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
